validator.source_text:
<scxml xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/07/scxml" version="1.0" initial="o">
  <state id="o">
    <transition event="go" target="h b1"/>
    <transition event="out" target="o"/>
  </state>
  <parallel id="p">
    <history id="h"><transition target="a"/></history>
    <state id="a"><state id="a1"/></state>
    <state id="b"><state id="b0"/><state id="b1"/></state>
    <transition event="out" target="o"/>
  </parallel>
</scxml>

diagnostics.message: transition targets `h` and `b1` can place the machine in an illegal configuration
notes: entering the history `h` enters its recorded (or default) configuration of `p` (SCXML 1.0 §3.10.2: "the SCXML processor MUST behave as if the transition had taken the stored state configuration for that history state as its target"); unless that configuration contains `b1`, the machine ends up with two active children of one state, and "A conformant SCXML document MUST place the state machine only in legal state configurations" (§3.11)
diagnostics.help: target either the history `h` or `b1`, not both
spec_references: SCXML 1.0 §3.11 Legal State Configurations and Specifications

diagnostics.message: compound state `b` has several child states but no explicit initial state

primary.message: entry behavior depends on implicit document order

secondary.message: entered first because it comes first in document order

notes: without `initial`, the first of several child states in document order is entered; reordering children silently changes behavior (a single child state is not reported)
diagnostics.help: make the entry explicit with `initial="b0"` (keeps the current behavior), or name the state that should be entered first

fixes.message: make the current entry state `b0` explicit
